pack.title: World History & Myth
pack.description: Gods, empires, wonders and the words that history left behind.

categories.title: GREEK GODS
categories.triviaFact: Poseidon was the Greek god of the sea, and also of earthquakes and horses.

categories.title: ANCIENT WONDERS
categories.triviaFact: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

categories.title: NASA PROGRAMS
categories.triviaFact: NASA's Artemis program is named after Apollo's twin sister in Greek mythology.

categories.title: WORDS FROM MYTH
categories.triviaFact: Tantalize comes from Tantalus, who was punished with food and water forever just out of reach.

redHerrings.note: ARTEMIS is a Greek goddess, but ZEUS, ATHENA, HERMES and POSEIDON already complete the gods; here ARTEMIS is NASA's Moon program.
MERCURY is the Roman counterpart of HERMES, but the gods on this board are Greek, and MERCURY was also NASA's first crewed program.

categories.title: EGYPTIAN GODS
categories.triviaFact: Anubis, the jackal-headed god, was linked with embalming and with guiding the souls of the dead.

categories.title: PHARAOHS
categories.triviaFact: Khufu commissioned the Great Pyramid of Giza, the largest of the pyramids there.

categories.title: WRITING SYSTEMS
categories.triviaFact: Ogham was an early medieval alphabet for Irish, carved as notches along the edges of standing stones.

categories.title: COMES BEFORE STONE
categories.triviaFact: Kissing the Blarney Stone in Ireland is said to grant the gift of eloquence.

redHerrings.note: ROSETTA feels Egyptian and helped decode writing, but HIEROGLYPH, CUNEIFORM, RUNES and OGHAM are the writing systems; ROSETTA comes before stone.

categories.title: ITALIAN CITIES
categories.triviaFact: Turin was the first capital of the unified Kingdom of Italy, from 1861 to 1865.

categories.title: LANDMARKS OF ROME
categories.triviaFact: The Pantheon's dome is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.

categories.title: NEW SEVEN WONDERS
categories.triviaFact: Petra in Jordan is famous for buildings carved directly into rose-colored sandstone cliffs.

categories.title: SPELLED WITH ROMAN NUMERALS
categories.triviaFact: These words use only I, V, X, L, C, D and M, the seven letters of standard Roman numerals.

redHerrings.note: The COLOSSEUM really is one of the New Seven Wonders, but PETRA, MACHU PICCHU, TAJ MAHAL and CHICHEN ITZA complete that group, and Rome needs its arena.

categories.title: QUEENS WHO RULED ENGLAND
categories.triviaFact: Queen Anne became the first monarch of Great Britain when England and Scotland united in 1707.

categories.title: ROYAL TITLES
categories.triviaFact: Tsar and kaiser both derive from Caesar, the family name of Rome's Julius Caesar.

categories.title: FAMOUS LAKES
categories.triviaFact: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake on Earth, reaching more than 1,600 meters.

categories.title: KING ___
categories.triviaFact: The king cobra is the world's longest venomous snake, sometimes exceeding five meters.

redHerrings.note: Lake VICTORIA is Africa's largest lake, but SUPERIOR, TITICACA, BAIKAL and GENEVA complete the lakes, and the queens need VICTORIA.

categories.title: NORSE GODS
categories.triviaFact: Thursday is named after Thor, and Wednesday after Woden, the Old English form of Odin.

categories.title: VIKING WORLD
categories.triviaFact: Viking longships had shallow hulls, letting them cross open seas and also sail far up rivers.

categories.title: MARVEL HEROES
categories.triviaFact: Wolverine first appeared in a 1974 issue of The Incredible Hulk before joining the X-Men.

categories.title: HIDDEN NORSE GODS
categories.triviaFact: Balderdash once meant a frothy jumble of mixed drinks before it came to mean nonsense.

redHerrings.note: THOR and LOKI are Marvel characters too, but HULK, IRON MAN, WOLVERINE and DAREDEVIL complete the heroes, leaving both with the Norse gods.
AUTHOR hides THOR, which can pull you toward the gods group, but the gods themselves appear as whole words.

categories.title: WORDS FROM ARABIC
categories.triviaFact: Algorithm comes from al-Khwarizmi, a Persian mathematician whose works were translated into Latin.

categories.title: WORDS FROM HINDI
categories.triviaFact: Shampoo comes from a Hindi word meaning to press or knead, first used for a head massage.

categories.title: WORDS NAMED AFTER PEOPLE
categories.triviaFact: Boycott is named after Charles Boycott, a land agent in Ireland who was shunned by his community in 1880.

categories.title: WORDS THAT BEGAN AS ACRONYMS
categories.triviaFact: Scuba stands for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus.

redHerrings.note: CARDIGAN and BANDANA are both things you wear, but CARDIGAN is named after the Earl of Cardigan, while BANDANA comes from Hindi.

categories.title: PHILOSOPHERS
categories.triviaFact: Socrates wrote nothing himself; his ideas survive mainly through the dialogues of his student Plato.

categories.title: FORMS OF GOVERNMENT
categories.triviaFact: Oligarchy comes from Greek words meaning rule by the few.

categories.title: GREEK CITY-STATES
categories.triviaFact: Corinth controlled a narrow isthmus, letting it profit from trade between two seas.

categories.title: WORDS FROM GREEK PLACES
categories.triviaFact: A meander takes its name from the winding Maeander River in what is now Turkey.

redHerrings.note: SPARTAN points straight at Sparta, a famous city-state, but the word is an adjective meaning austere; ATHENS, THEBES, CORINTH and ARGOS are the cities.
REPUBLIC is also the title of Plato's best-known dialogue, but here it is a form of government.

categories.title: CIVILIZATIONS OF THE AMERICAS
categories.triviaFact: The Olmec carved colossal stone heads, some standing around three meters tall.

categories.title: ANCIENT CITIES
categories.triviaFact: Pompeii was buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE and rediscovered in the 1700s.

categories.title: EPIC POEMS
categories.triviaFact: Beowulf survives in a single manuscript, which was damaged in a library fire in 1731.

categories.title: ___ CALENDAR
categories.triviaFact: The Gregorian calendar, introduced in 1582, skips leap days in most century years.

redHerrings.note: The MAYA and AZTEC calendars are famous, but GREGORIAN, JULIAN, LUNAR and ADVENT complete the calendars; both peoples belong with the civilizations.
TROY is the setting of the ILIAD, but it is an ancient city here, not a poem.
